headline: High risk of capability conflict and cascading errors: MinerU can feed document outputs into transformers pipelines, while both agents expose overlapping file and API surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU ingests PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, OCR text and exposes an MCP server; transformers can consume stdin/stdout, example scripts, and model files. A prompt-injection path exists if MinerU output is manually or programmatically bridged into a transformers pipeline, but no shared channel is documented by default.
conditions: IF MinerU output is copied into a transformers prompt or script input without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF an MCP or file bridge is configured between the two agents, attacker-controlled document text can reach transformers as instructions.
mitigations: Disable any automatic handoff from MinerU outputs to transformers prompts.
Wrap MinerU output in a fixed schema before passing it onward.
Add a delimiter and instruction-stripping step in the pipeline.
Review one sample document-to-prompt path for prompt-like text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all MinerU outputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU touches PDFs, images, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX and can call APIs including an MCP server; transformers reads files, model files, and example scripts and has broad network egress. If they share a workspace, document contents can flow from MinerU into transformers and then out through networked inference or hub calls, creating a default-configuration leakage path.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or directory, document contents can be exposed to transformers.
IF transformers is configured to upload or serve processed inputs, those contents can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Separate workspaces for each agent.
Turn off transformers network egress for sensitive runs.
Use redacted sample files when testing the pair.
Check whether MinerU outputs contain secrets before handoff.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MinerU supports concurrent inference and exposes file/API surfaces; transformers has execute_shell, install_packages, read/write filesystem, subprocesses, and broad network egress. If both are pointed at the same directory or model artifacts, they can overwrite or race on shared files, and the uncertainty is not enough to downgrade because the write surface is explicit on transformers and MinerU can still interact via APIs/files.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file races or corruption can occur.
IF transformers scripts modify shared model or output files while MinerU is running, state conflicts are likely.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Run only one writer at a time on shared artifacts.
Make shared paths read-only for MinerU.
Use file locks around any common workspace.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces extracted text, tables, formulas, and OCR output; transformers can consume those artifacts in pipelines and example scripts. That makes MinerU's output a plausible upstream input to transformers, and without a verification step transformers may treat extraction errors as authoritative, causing downstream mistakes in generated documents or code.
conditions: IF transformers uses MinerU extraction as direct pipeline input, extraction errors can propagate.
IF downstream scripts trust MinerU OCR or table output without validation, incorrect facts can be acted on.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before downstream use.
Compare extracted fields against source documents for a sample set.
Require confidence thresholds before passing data onward.
Log provenance for each extracted field.
requires-engineering: add automated validation against source PDFs.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and list no secrets handled or special regulated scopes, so there is no documented residency or certification mismatch in the profiles. The main compliance concern is operational logging/retention, but that is not evidenced here; the pair itself does not show a clear residency breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either agent's workspace, separate compliance review is required.
IF deployment logging retains extracted documents beyond policy, retention controls must be applied.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in test runs.
Confirm retention settings for any logs.
Document the data classes allowed in the shared workflow.
Use synthetic documents for validation.
requires-engineering: add policy-based retention enforcement.
